label: rejected

evidence.V1: Top and three-quarter read as a paved floor; front and silhouette are a plain slab with a faintly notched top edge.
evidence.V2: Running-bond stones give a clear medium layer, but there is no small detail (chips, worn corners) and the base slab is empty; some hierarchy.
evidence.V3: All stones are perfect rectangles of identical height in a regular bond; reads as machined pavers rather than stylised flagstones.
evidence.V4: Stone tops have consistent chamfers that catch light (close_flagstones_studio), but the base slab corners are razor sharp (close_edge_studio); inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups show clean bevels and gaps with no z-fighting, pinching or stray facets.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 2-3 values, consistent across granite/brick/sandstone/slate/basalt; the darker values are clustered in one corner row rather than scattered.
evidence.V8: Vertex colour and chamfered stones match the kit; unchamfered base and lack of hand-made irregularity are a minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (Box collision, grid-corner pivot, white colour); T1 passes (Y iou 0.986).

top_fixes: Give stones slight size/height/rotation variation and a few chipped corners so they read as stylised flagstones
Scatter the dark-value stones across the tile instead of one clustered row (avoids a visible stripe when tiled)
Chamfer the base slab edges or recess it so the sides are not a flat razor box
